title: Consumer Expectations Survey Report: 1st Quarter 2026
authors: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, Department of Economic Statistics
tldr: Quarterly survey of 5,358 Filipino households reveals improved but still pessimistic consumer confidence (-15.8% CI), with 56.2% planning to save, 73.9% allocating less than 10% of income to savings, and strong reliance on OFW remittances for food (96.1%) and education (69.9%).
problem_and_motivation: The BSP Consumer Expectations Survey tracks quarterly household sentiment on economic conditions, family finances, spending, savings, and borrowing to inform monetary policy. The Q1 2026 survey captures consumer outlook prior to the US-Israel-Iran conflict, providing baseline Philippine household financial behavior data across income groups.
approach: Stratified multi-stage probability sampling of 5,440 eligible households from the PSA 2023 Geo-Enabled Master Sample.
5,358 households participated (98.5% response rate): 2,434 from NCR and 2,924 from AONCR.
Income group classification: Low (<₱10,000/mo), Middle (₱10,000-₱29,999/mo), High (>₱30,000/mo).
Confidence Index (CI) computed as percentage affirmative minus percentage negative responses.
Diffusion Index used for inflation rate, peso borrowing rate, exchange rate, and unemployment rate expectations.
findings: num: -15.8% overall consumer confidence index for Q1 2026 (improved from -22.2% in Q4 2025).
num: 56.2% of households plan to set aside savings in Q1 2026 (up from 52.3% in Q4 2025).
num: 73.9% of saving households allocate less than 10% of monthly income to savings.
num: 96.1% of OFW households use remittances for food and household needs.
num: 69.9% of OFW households allocate remittances to education, 66.0% to medical expenses.
num: 40.2% of OFW households allocate remittances to savings.
num: 2.7% year-ahead inflation forecast (within BSP's 3.0% target ±1.0pp tolerance).
num: -69.5% borrowing intention index for Q2 2026 (improved from -71.7%).
num: 19.0% of households plan to apply for a loan in the next 12 months.
num: 58.6% of households prefer properties priced at ₱450,000 and below.
Low-income group shows most pessimistic outlook (-24.7% CI) compared to high-income (-7.9% CI).
NCR consumers slightly more pessimistic (-18.2%) than AONCR (-15.4%) for current quarter.
Spending outlook declined from 43.7% to 40.3%, less upbeat across most categories except water/electricity.
Family financial situation CI improved significantly from -14.6% to -6.2%.
Savings intention index turned positive at 12.4% (first time in the series from Q1 2021).

definitions.definition: Computed as percentage of households answering affirmative minus percentage answering negative for a given indicator. Positive CI indicates favorable view, except for inflation and borrowing rates where positive indicates opposite.

Index measuring the direction of change in economic indicators. +/- indicates more respondents expect increase/decrease. Used for inflation rate, peso borrowing rate, exchange rate, and unemployment rate expectations.
Households with monthly family income of less than ₱10,000.
Households with monthly family income between ₱10,000 and ₱29,999.
Households with monthly family income of more than ₱30,000.
Net balance approach: difference between percentage of households with intention to save and percentage with no intention to save. Positive value indicates more households plan to save.
Net balance approach: difference between percentage of households with intention to apply for a loan and percentage with no intention. Negative value indicates fewer households plan to borrow.
Money sent by Overseas Filipino Workers to their households in the Philippines. Income estimation includes OFW remittances received in the last 12 months starting Q1 2019.

topics.name: Behavioral and Psychological Aspects of Personal Finance
topics.justification: Directly measures Filipino household financial sentiment, savings behavior, and spending intentions across income groups — core behavioral data for understanding how households perceive and manage their finances.

topics.name: Patterns of Personal Financial Behavior
topics.justification: Provides empirical data on savings allocation (73.9% save <10% of income), spending priorities, and borrowing intentions across income strata.

topics.name: Barriers to Effective Financial Management
topics.justification: Identifies income-based disparities: low-income group most pessimistic (-24.7% CI vs -7.9% high-income), showing structural barriers to financial well-being.

topics.name: Landscape of Existing Personal Finance Systems
topics.justification: Documents the current state of Filipino household finances: OFW remittance dependence (96.1% for food), property affordability preferences (58.6% at ₱450K and below), and debt sentiment.

topics.name: Incentive Mechanisms and Behavioral Nudges
topics.justification: Savings intention turned positive (12.4%) — first time in survey history — suggesting potential responsiveness to financial incentive mechanisms.

topics.name: Financial Behavioral Profiles in Personal Finance Systems
topics.justification: Provides income-based behavioral profiling: low-income (66.2% saving <5% of income), middle-income (47.5% <5%), high-income (35.9% <5%).

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This BSP quarterly survey provides authoritative baseline data on Filipino household financial behavior, directly informing the Odin thesis context. It documents key behavioral patterns: the dominance of food/household spending (96.1% of OFW remittances), extremely low savings rates (73.9% save <10% of income), and stark income-based disparities (low-income group CI at -24.7% vs high-income at -7.9%). The Q1 2026 data captures a critical inflection point — savings intention turned positive (12.4%) for the first time in the series, while consumer confidence remained deeply pessimistic (-15.8%). These findings establish the empirical foundation for understanding why a personal budget management system like Odin is needed in the Philippine context.

limits: Quarterly snapshot — does not capture longitudinal individual financial behavior changes.
Survey-based sentiment data may suffer from response bias and social desirability effects.
Income group classification is broad (three tiers) and based on estimated household income.
Savings data beginning Q1 2025 uses only forward-looking questions due to BSP survey streamlining.
No granular data on specific financial products, digital payment usage, or budgeting practices.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 1 (Behavioral/ Psychological Aspects) was flagged as high relevance because the CES directly measures Filipino household financial sentiment, savings behavior, and spending intentions — core behavioral data. Domain 3 (Patterns of Personal Financial Behavior) was flagged as high relevance for its empirical documentation of savings allocation (73.9% save <10%) and spending priorities. Domain 3 (Barriers) was flagged as high relevance for documenting income-based disparities. Domain 4 (Landscape of Existing Systems) was flagged as medium relevance for its characterization of the current financial landscape including OFW remittance dependence. Domain 7 (Incentive Mechanisms/Nudges) was flagged as medium relevance because the first positive savings intention index (12.4%) suggests potential responsiveness to financial interventions. Domain 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles) was flagged as medium relevance for its income-based behavioral profiling. Domains 2, 6, 8-14 were considered and rejected as this survey does not address AI/ML systems, budgeting system features, expense categorization, data privacy, or system design.

limitations: No granular financial product or digital payment data.
remember_this: 73.9% of Filipino households save less than 10% of their monthly income — a critical barrier to financial resilience.
Low-income households (<₱10K/mo) have the most pessimistic outlook at -24.7% CI, 3x worse than high-income (-7.9%).
OFW remittances are overwhelmingly used for survival (96.1% food/household needs), not wealth building.
Savings intention turned positive (12.4%) for the first time in the CES series — a potential inflection point.
19% of households plan to borrow in the next 12 months, with borrowing intention improving but still deeply negative.
